How a search box becomes a paid order — designing the PLP, PDP, cart and checkout, plus the SEO, i18n and performance

10 min read
Just now

--

Press enter or click to view image in full size

E-commerce looks like the friendly system design prompt. Everybody has seen a product page. “Build Flipkart’s frontend” — how hard can it be? Then the follow-ups land. How does the cart survive a refresh for a guest user? Why isn’t your listing page showing up on Google? Where exactly does the final price get calculated? Suddenly the easy prompt is a two-hour conversation, because on an e-commerce frontend the money literally changes hands on the client — and every decision you make has a rupee value attached to it.
Most interviews open with something deceptively broad: design the frontend for an e-commerce app. The trap is to start drawing boxes immediately. The signal the interviewer is actually looking for is whether you can take a giant, vague product and carve out the part that matters, justify what you left out, and then reason about the hard bits — rendering, state, SEO, performance — like someone who has shipped this before.
Let me walk through how I’d drive that round end to end.
1. Requirements
